question.text: Priya invests Rs. 10,000 at the beginning of each month in a mutual fund SIP earning 12% p.a. for 15 years. Using an annuity-due (beginning-of-month) calculation, the approximate corpus at the end of 15 years is:

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook FV formulas depend on whether payments are made at the beginning or end of the period. For a beginning-of-month SIP, FV (annuity due) = PMT × [((1+r)^n - 1) / r] × (1+r). With PMT = 10,000, r = 1% per month, n = 180 months, this gives approximately Rs. 50,45,760. (An end-of-month SIP with the same inputs gives approximately Rs. 49,95,802.) The Trap: Rs. 18,00,000 is the simple sum of principal invested (10,000 × 12 × 15) — it ignores returns entirely and is the typical anchoring trap. Note: SIP corpus is sensitive to the payment-timing assumption — annuity due (beginning) gives a slightly higher FV than ordinary annuity (end) because each instalment earns one extra month of return.
